in_hebrew.name: עזיקאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עזיקאל הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'אלוהים יחזק' או 'אלוהים יאמץ אותי'. השם עזיקאל מורכב משתי מילים: 'עז' שפירושו 'אלוהים' ו'יקאל' שפירושו 'יחזק' או 'יאמץ'. השם עזיקאל מוזכר במקרא בספר יחזקאל, הנביא שכתב את הספר הנושא את שמו.

in_greek.name: Εζεκιήλ
in_greek.meaning: ο Θεός θα δυναμώσει - ο Θεός θα ενδυναμώσει
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Εζεκιήλ είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος עזיקאל, που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός θα δυναμώσει' ή 'ο Θεός θα ενδυναμώσει'. Το όνομα Εζεκιήλ αναφέρεται στο βιβλίο του προφήτη Εζεκιήλ στην Καινή Διαθήκη.

in_latin.name: Ezequiel

in_english.name: Ezequiel

in_english.long_meaning: The name Ezequiel is derived from the Hebrew name עזיקאל (Ezequiel), which means 'God will strengthen' or 'God will empower'. The name Ezequiel is composed of two elements: 'El' (God) and 'kachel' (to strengthen). In the Christian tradition, Ezequiel is associated with the prophet Ezekiel, who wrote the book of Ezekiel in the Old Testament. The name Ezequiel has been used in various Christian cultures, particularly in Spanish and Portuguese-speaking countries.

data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, the name Ezequiel holds great importance for those who believe in God's divine intervention and guidance in human affairs. The name evokes a sense of trust and faith in God's strength and power, reflecting the biblical story of a prophet who was chosen by God to carry His message to His people despite the challenges and adversities he faced. data.spiritual_symbolism: Ezequiel, meaning "God will strengthen," is a name that embodies faith and divine support. biblical_reference.note: The prophet Ezekiel wrote the book of Ezekiel, which is one of the major prophetic books in the Old Testament.

historical_references.reference: Ezequiel is mentioned in the Old Testament Book of Ezekiel, which was written between 593-571 BCE during the Babylonian exile of the Israelites in Babylon. He is described as a priest and a scribe from the priestly family of Zadok.

According to the New Testament Book of Matthew (8:1-4), a centurion from Capernaum named Ezequiel asked Jesus to heal his slave. This event is believed to have occurred around 27 CE during Jesus' ministry in Galilee.
